All resources, fields, endpoints, metrics and events in this workbook form proposed AMLOK v0.1.0. They are not a statement that integrations are deployed.
Schema approval and contract tests are release gates.
Normalized union of credit-relevant fields across 238 inventory entries, plus Didit, Baselayer and PPSA Canada. Provider-specific extras use documented namespaced extensions.
This is not an exhaustive dump of every vendor API field.
Documented means an upstream field was visible in reviewed public documentation. Candidate means it needs provider/schema validation. Neither means production-tested or licensed.
See Field Mappings and Provider Coverage.
Required describes a valid AMLOK resource when that resource exists. It does not guarantee a source supplies every optional field or that every resource exists.
Required source IDs must be resolved or the record is quarantined.
Every top-level resource inherits common fields. Resource-name prefixes in Field Dictionary are documentation context; response data contains the relative field names.
Shared Types expands every reusable nested object.

Use null for known missing/unavailable optional values and include missing_fields reasons. Zero and false require evidence. An empty array means the requested collection was queried and is known empty.
Denied sensitive fields are omitted; missing_fields may explain redaction without exposing values.
Dates preserve their source calendar date. Timestamps use RFC 3339 UTC with original timezone in provenance where needed. Date-only evidence is never padded into an invented timestamp.
posted_on, observed_at, effective_at and retrieved_at remain distinct.
Money uses exact decimal strings in major currency units and a currency code. Convert minor-unit sources using currency-specific exponent tables. Preserve higher precision when source requires it.
No binary floating-point financial calculations; do not assume all currencies have two decimals.
Bank transaction amount is an absolute magnitude with separate direction. Processor ledger net and gross can be signed. Loan principal is an obligation magnitude.
Convert per provider and product; do not use one global sign rule.
Rates and proportions are decimal fractions: 9.5% is 0.095. DSCR and current ratio are multiples, not percentages.
Units and denominator policies are required.
Keep original money. Cross-currency aggregates require an explicit FX source, effective time, rate convention and rounding method.
Never sum CAD and USD without stated conversion.
AMLOK IDs are opaque and tenant-scoped. Provider identifiers remain case-sensitive strings qualified by provider, connection and resource type.
Preserve leading zeroes; masks and names are not keys.
Preserve original spelling, scripts and address text. Store matching normalization as a separate versioned transformation.
No automatic merge on fuzzy name similarity alone.
Normalize countries to alpha-2 where verified. Preserve jurisdiction, source code and taxonomy version for registry and industry fields.
NAICS, SIC, MCC and NACE are not interchangeable.
Relationships require evidence. Keep unresolved counterparties and review state rather than forcing a legal-entity match.
Canonical merging must be reversible and audited.
Deduplicate within a source using stable keys. Link cross-source order, invoice, payment, payout and bank records with reconciliation evidence.
These records describe different economic stages and must not be summed as independent revenue.
Use purpose-specific authoritative sources, observation dates and review state. Preserve conflicting values in provenance.
A registry source may establish formation; a borrower assertion cannot silently overwrite it as verified.
Use source cursors/webhooks where available. Store record versions, pending-to-posted linkage, removals and immutable assessment input manifests.
AMLOK change cursors are separate from provider cursors.
Return actual time span, sources, account set and jurisdictions completed. Failed or unqueried sources remain explicit.
Partial success never becomes a completed no-hit result.
Provider update frequency, AMLOK polling, ingestion time and source effective time are distinct.
No universal real-time or historical-depth promise.

Restricted fields use explicit entitlements and purpose. Default identifiers are masked or tokenized. Raw biometric media, PAN, CVV and provider credentials are excluded from the normalized default response.
Per-client retention, residency and access policies must be implemented.
Every computed value records inputs, window, unit, calculation/model version and evidence coverage. Missing prerequisites produce unavailable status.
No invented credit score, PD, fraud probability or approved limit.
Use a configured AMLOK API_BASE_URL; no production hostname is declared in this draft. Paths begin /v1.
Proposed server-to-server bearer API keys, separately issued for sandbox and production, scoped to one institution tenant. OAuth can be added as a separately specified mechanism.
Never accept tenant identity solely from a caller-supplied tenant_id.
Enforce tenant ownership plus resource scope and field entitlements on every request, linked object and event delivery.
Read permissions do not authorize borrower communications or payment execution.
Single item: {data: resource, meta: ResponseMeta}. List: {data: [resource], page: Page, meta: ResponseMeta}. Error: {error: Error, meta: ResponseMeta}.
No provider credentials or unsafe raw upstream error payloads.
Cursor pagination with proposed default limit 100 and maximum 200; stable order by updated_at then id. Cursors bind filters, tenant and snapshot.
has_more=false and next_cursor=null at the end.
Only documented filters are supported. Reject unknown or invalid filters; do not silently return broader records.
Date intervals are start-inclusive and end-exclusive unless a field explicitly says inclusive.
as_of applies only where a point-in-time snapshot exists. Otherwise return unsupported_parameter; do not relabel current records as historical.
Require Idempotency-Key for POST commands. Proposed retention 24 hours, scoped by tenant and operation; replay identical request, reject differing body with 409.
Retention is a draft policy, not a current SLA.
Mutable configuration uses If-Match with record version/ETag. Reject stale updates with 412.
No silent last-writer-wins for policy or approved actions.
Long-running commands return 202 with a resource ID and polling URL. The accepted result is not a completed decision.
Completion or partial failure is observable through polling and events.
Enforce tenant and provider-aware limits. Return 429 with Retry-After. Numeric contractual quotas remain to be set.
Use bounded exponential backoff with jitter.
Use stable codes; 400 bad input, 401 unauthenticated, 403 entitlement, 404 missing/not visible, 409 conflict, 412 stale version, 422 invalid semantics, 429 throttled, 502/503 upstream, 500 internal.
Breaking field type, meaning or requiredness changes require a new contract version. Additive optional fields preserve existing semantics; enum additions must be announced.
Clients retain raw provider status and handle unknown normalized enum values where defined.
Proposed at-least-once delivery; consumers deduplicate event IDs. Arrival order is not guaranteed; resource_version prevents stale overwrite.
Fetch authoritative authorized resource after receiving event.
Proposed HMAC-SHA256 of timestamp + period + exact raw body, using a dedicated webhook secret. Header X-AMLOK-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>.
Constant-time comparison; proposed 5-minute tolerance and event-ID replay prevention.
Proposed retry schedule: 1m, 5m, 30m, 2h, 8h and 24h after first failure. Log terminal delivery failure and expose replay.
2xx acknowledges; no numeric reliability SLA asserted.
Deliver resource references and limited status changes by default; retrieve sensitive evidence through authenticated reads.
Tenant-bound destination, HTTPS and SSRF validation required.
POST /documents uses multipart upload or approved pre-signed upload flow. Validate actual MIME, size, malware and tenant ownership.
Max upload size and residency policy require release configuration.
Sending messages, filing liens, initiating money movement and changing credit limits require separately authorized command routes and approvals.
This draft includes approved communication dispatch, but no payment initiation or lien filing API.
Revoke consent stops future collection. Deletion requests run an auditable retention/legal-hold process and return a job, not an immediate promise to erase every provider copy.
Deletion propagation depends on provider contract and applicable retention policy.
Contract approval, per-provider schema validation, sandbox tests, coverage verification, commercial data rights, security review and tenant isolation are required before published availability.
